items.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023
items.q: He also went and played lead for Quincy Jones in that first Quincy Jones band that went overseas with Sarah Vaughan.

ctx.x: Is the atmosphere at Berklee more like a family? Were you, I’m trying to get this idea about the academic level. Was it less about testing and goals than it was about just learning to play gigs?

You know what made Berklee, to me, was the humanity of the faculty in 1965, ’66, actually go back to ’55. I go back a whole lot more years. But when I went to the New England Conservatory in 1955, jazz was a dirty word. It was the popular department and there were a few of us, like Roger Kellaway, the great pianist, and Freddie Buda, the percussionist for the Pops, great drummer, and myself and a few others, Al Nathan, were into jazz and we just were not interested in going immediately into the symphony. That was…

284 Newbury Street, it’s a brown house — that’s the Berklee School of Music and there’s no degree given out. You can get a diploma. And all of a sudden you have teachers like Lennie Johnson — Lennie Johnson was a lead trumpet player you probably never heard of, but when Cat Anderson got shall we say, took a vacation to get his head back together, Lennie Johnson went out and covered for him for six weeks. And this was a regular happening over and over. So that in itself was a family. Lennie taught Bill Chase and…
